text: dsh-md-live 是一款面向 DSH Web 的 Markdown 工作区阅读与编辑插件。它在右侧栏注册 md-live 标签页，可浏览工作区中的 Markdown 文件、搜索和打开文档，并在文件变化时刷新预览。面板渲染 Markdown 内容，支持编辑后保存回原文件；Agent 请求展示 Markdown 时也可打开相应文件。适合在 DSH 对话旁阅读、检查和修改项目文档。安装命令为 dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-md-live。

dsh-md-live adds a Markdown tab to the DSH Web right sidebar. It browses and previews workspace Markdown files, refreshes when files change, and lets users edit and save a document. Install with `dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-md-live`.
想在 DSH 对话旁边打开并预览工作区里的 Markdown 文档。
工作区的 Markdown 文件更新后，能不能自动刷新右侧预览？
I want to edit a workspace Markdown file and save it from the DSH sidebar.
dsh-md-live 的功能「Markdown 阅读与实时预览」：在 DSH Web 右侧栏浏览并打开工作区 Markdown 文件，读取内容后渲染为预览；文件变化时通过工作区变更流更新显示。
dsh-md-live 的功能「编辑并保存 Markdown」：在面板中编辑当前 Markdown 文本并保存回原文件，写入时携带版本信息，返回保存或版本已变化等结果。

dsh-md-live README · dsh-md-live：**Live Markdown preview and editor for the DSH Web right sidebar**

Open a `.md` beside the conversation: it redraws itself as the file changes, can be edited and saved in place, and turns a selected paragraph into a quote in the composer.

dsh-md-live README · dsh-md-live：[Quick start](#quick-start) · [Features](#features) · [Usage](#usage) · [How it works](#how-it-works) · [Development](#development) · [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md) · [中文](README.zh.md) > **In one line** — a workspace Markdown tab that renders GFM, KaTeX and highlighted code, follows the files the Agent writes, saves through the Session's sandbox, and quotes a passage into the composer.

dsh-md-live README · Quick start：```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-md-live
```

Restart the harness and reload the page. Reloading the page alone is not enough: the Host half is composed when `dsh web` boots, so install with the server stopped, or stop and start it afterwards. The `dsh.client` declaration in `package.json` makes the Host serve `lib/client.cjs` as this package's Client half automatically — no extra patch row is needed.

dsh-md-live README · Quick start：Then click `+` at the top of the right sidebar, pick **md-live**, and choose a `.md` from the workspace.

> **Requires** DSH ≥ 0.2.1-rc.2. The published tarball ships both halves already built, so installing needs no Node.js toolchain; React comes from DSH's browser module table.

dsh-md-live README · From source：```bash
git clone https://github.com/lg114/dsh-md-live.git
cd dsh-md-live
npm install
npm run build

Building needs Node.js ≥ 18.
dsh-md-live README · Features：The Client half does the work. The Host half adds only two things: the `preview_md` tool and the write Remote.

dsh-md-live README · Finding a document：- **A real right-Sidebar tab** — registered through `ctx.sidebarRightTabs` + `sidebar.right.pane.tab`, the same mechanism as the Files and Terminal tabs. It is not a panel shoved into the main column.
- **Whole-workspace scan** — walks the entire tree from the Session's workspace root, eight listings in flight per level, drawing results level by level: the first level shows up while the rest is still being walked.
- **Editable filter rules** — `node_modules`, `.git`, `dist` and friends are skipped by default; the rules are edited in the panel, remembered per browser, and can be cleared to scan everything.
- **Search and recents** — filter the workspace list by any fragment of the path; the documents you opened last sit at the top.
- **The path is visible** — the header shows `directory/filename` relative to the workspace, with the absolute path in the tooltip. In a narrow panel the directory gives way first; the filename never truncates.
- **Open it elsewhere** — hand the file to the OS default application, or reveal it in the file manager, straight from the header.

dsh-md-live README · Reading：- **Live refresh** — driven by `remote.workspaceFiles.changes`. A manual refresh button only appears when watching turns out to be unavailable.
- **Table of contents** — headings are extracted and their ids injected at render time, so the entries actually scroll. The heading you are reading is marked as you scroll, and the column folds to a rail when the panel is narrow.
- **Images beside the document** — a relative `` path is resolved against the file's own directory and served by the Host's file endpoint, so a screenshot sitting next to the `.md` actually shows up. Click an image to open it full size.
- **Links do what they look like** — a link to another `.md` opens it in this tab, `#anchor` scrolls inside the document, and an `https://` link goes to the browser instead of navigating the app away.

dsh-md-live README · Rendering：- **Safe rendering** — sanitised by DOMPurify (HTML profile): scripts, iframes, event attributes and `javascript:` URLs are stripped.
- **Syntax highlighting** — highlight.js with 27 languages registered on demand.
- **Math** — `$inline$` and `$$display$$` go through KaTeX. The output is MathML rather than KaTeX's own HTML: the HTML rendering needs KaTeX's web fonts, several hundred kilobytes the plugin has no way to serve, so the browser draws the maths itself.
- **Code blocks you can act on** — every block shows its language and a copy control on hover. The copy drops the trailing newline, so a pasted command does not run itself.
- **Front matter stays metadata** — a leading `---` block is lifted out of the prose and shown in a collapsed box, instead of turning into a stray horizontal rule and a `title: …` paragraph.

dsh-md-live README · Editing：- **Edit and save in place** — **Edit** turns the document into a textarea over the same file; **Save** (or `Ctrl/Cmd+S`) writes it back through the Host, under the Session's own sandbox policy. Saving is optimistic: the request carries the version the editor started from, and a file that changed underneath raises a dialog with **Overwrite** and **Reload** instead of quietly losing one side.
- **Drafts are guarded** — the back arrow, another file from the picker, an Agent-follow switch and a browser unload all ask before they drop a draft, and a live update never overwrites a dirty one.

dsh-md-live README · Working with the Agent：- **Follows the Agent, even with the panel closed** — when the Agent finishes writing a `.md` inside the workspace, the panel opens on that file. The subscription is plugin-level and fed by `remote.session.follow` for whichever Session is on screen, so it works whether or not a tab was already open. The switch waits for `tool/result` rather than `tool/call`, so the file is read after the write landed instead of before it. One checkbox in the panel settings turns it off.
- **The Agent can ask, not just write** — a `preview_md` tool lets it put a document on screen on request ("show me the notes"). It is honoured even when automatic following is off, because that one was asked for.
- **Quote into the conversation** — select text in the preview and an **Add to conversation** pill appears under it. One click puts the excerpt into this Session's composer as a blockquote with its source path, at the caret, and focuses the input; the draft, its @ references and whatever you had already typed stay exactly as they were. A draft that changed in the same instant is reported instead of overwritten.

dsh-md-live README · Fitting into the app：- **Reading settings** — body size, leading and measure, remembered per browser. Every default is "follow the app", so the panel still obeys the app's own Markdown tokens until you say otherwise.
- **Follows the app's settings** — colours, font sizes and font families all read DSH's `--dsw-*` design tokens, so the light/dark appearance, the font-size stepper and any registered third-party theme carry over.
- **Speaks the app's language** — the panel's copy is one `md-live` locale namespace with `zh` and `en` dictionaries, so it follows the language picked in Settings → General and switches live: the slot renderer re-renders the body and the chip with a new `t` seat, no reload. Refusals travel as codes from the Host, so even a sandbox denial is phrased in the reader's language instead of arriving in the Host's Chinese.

dsh-md-live README · Usage：1. Click `+` at the top of the right sidebar, pick **md-live**, then a `.md` from the list.
2. To switch files, click `←` to the left of the title.
3. **Edit** changes the file in place; `Ctrl/Cmd+S` saves; **Preview** goes back.
4. Select text in the preview for the **Add to conversation** pill; `Esc` dismisses it.

dsh-md-live README · Usage：The `Skipped N directories (M rules)` line at the bottom of the picker opens the rule editor: one directory name per line. Saving rescans immediately; **Restore defaults** brings back the built-in list; **Show everything** clears the rules, so `.md` files inside `node_modules` are listed too.

Rules live in `localStorage` under `dsh-md-live.skip-dirs.v1` — per browser, never written back to the profile config.

dsh-md-live README · How it works：```text Client (everything happens here) ├── tab type sidebarRightTabs.register({ id, kind, title, guide }) ├── body/title keyed slots, key = id ├── file list remote.workspaceFiles.list BFS by level + concurrency + progressive Most of the design is constraints that only show up at runtime:
Eight constraints, each learned the hard way

dsh-md-live README · How it works：1. **`ctx.remote.*` returns a Result envelope**, not a bare value: `{ ok: true, value } | { ok: false, error }`. Reading fields off it yields `undefined` *without throwing* — which is exactly how an empty file list looks like an empty workspace.
2. **`list` / `readBytes` reject an empty path** with `path is required`. The scan must start from the Session's absolute cwd (the slot's standard prop `useSessions` → `byId[sessionId].cwd`).
3. **`changes` is a Remote stream**: wrap it in `remote.$stream({ name, open, ended })` and `accept()` every frame, or the uplink window fills and live updates stop silently.
4. **There is no Host → Client event bridge — but there is a Session stream.** `ctx.emit` on the Host never reaches the browser. What a Client *can* observe is `remote.session.follow`: a Remote stream carrying the Session's own events, `tool/call` and `tool/result` among them. That stream is the only reason "follow what the Agent writes" works at all, and it is why the Host half can stay empty.
5. **A client bundle must be `window.__ModuleLoader__.load({ id, factory })`**: executing the script only registers a factory, and the loader supplies `req

dsh-md-live README · Write path：`mdLive/writeText` is a custom Typert Remote because `workspaceFiles` exposes no mutation. Its wire signature is four positional parameters — `writeText(sessionId, path, content, version)` — and the first one is a `session` **lookup**, not a payload field: the Gateway resolves the id to the live Session through the registry entry `dsh-session` owns, so the Host method receives the Session itself. The browser cannot name a mode or a root; it only selects whose rules apply.

dsh-md-live README · Write path：1. `ctx.sandboxPolicy.resolve({ session })` supplies the mode (the Session's `sandbox/mode` event, else the deployment default `DSH_PERMISSION_MODE ?? workspace-write`) and the writable root (`session.header.cwd`).
2. That policy is passed as `fs.writeText`'s fifth argument. `SandboxedFileSystem` re-canonicalises the target and checks containment against it — or refuses outright in `read-only`, or skips the fence in `danger-full-access`.
3. Omitting the argument is the bug this replaced: the backend then falls back to the deployment policy, whose root is the Host process's **cwd**, so every file outside the directory `dsh web` was launched from is refused — including the Session's own workspace.

dsh-md-live README · Write path：Every fallback errs toward refusing: an unresolved lookup is retried as a plain id through `ctx.get('sessions')`; a Session that is gone is refused instead of guessed at; a composition without a `sandboxPolicy` service (plain `fs-local`) passes `undefined` and keeps the backend's behaviour; unrecognised I/O failures surface verbatim. What the write path deliberately does not do is widen its own authority — no retry against another root, no promotion to `danger-full-access`, no mode or root accepted from the client.

dsh-md-live README · Development：| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `npm run build` | Host (`tsc`) + Client (`esbuild`) |
| `npm run build:client` | Client only |
| `npm run verify` | Both suites, Host first |
| `npm run verify:client` | Mount the built bundle in jsdom — 92 checks |
| `npm run verify:host` | Run the built Host half against a fake context — 28 checks |
| `npm run clean` | Remove `lib/` |

dsh-md-live README · Development：`verify:client` simulates DSH's module loader (register → materialize → `apply`), then mounts the tab body in jsdom. It covers registration and slot keys, unwrapping the Remote envelope, directory recursion, filter rules and their persistence, progressive rendering, live refresh, unmount cleanup, TOC anchors, sanitisation, highlighting, image and link resolution, the Host opener calls, search, recents, outline folding, reading settings, the code toolbar, front matter, following the Agent's writes, math, locale switching, the quote pill, the navigation guard, and the editor: dirty tracking, save, and the stale-version dialog. Run it after changing client code — it is far faster than clicking through the browser.

dsh-md-live README · Development：`verify:host` imports the built Host half and calls `apply` with a fake cordis context: what it injects, the tool's schema, the arguments it refuses, the descriptor's wire parameters, the per-call sandbox policy it forwards, how a denial is worded, and that a registry which throws costs the tool rather than the plugin. It cannot exercise a real Agent turn — that still needs the browser.

dsh-md-live README · Development：Two files at the repository root are for the browser check rather than for the tests: `test.md` is a manual checklist (frontmatter, three code blocks, a relative image that also exercises a `..` path, four kinds of link, anchors, tables and lists) and `test-image.png` is the image it points at. Open `test.md` in the panel after a rendering change — that is the one thing `verify:client` cannot cover.

dsh-md-live README · Known limitations：- **Writes go through a custom Remote, not `workspaceFiles`**: `workspaceFiles` has no mutation API, so `mdLive/writeText` supplies one (see [Write path](#write-path)). Saving needs a *live* Session, because the mode and the root are both resolved from it; a Session that is not live is refused rather than written with a guessed mode. The Session id is client-supplied — a selector, not an authorization, since the Host alone decides the mode and root. That is also the official model: `workspaceFileScope` is a lookup over a client-supplied id, and DSH authenticates the *caller* (an owner Peer behind the Host/Origin fence, plus a process token), not which Session a call belongs to. A Remote handler never sees the Peer, so a plugin cannot tighten this by itself.
- **Following reads tool arguments, not the filesystem**: a `.md` the Agent rewrites through `bash` (`cat > x.md`, a heredoc) is not followed, because that call carries no path. `write`, `edit` and `str_replace_editor` are.
- **A draft cannot survive the tab being closed with its `×`**: the right Sidebar offers no per-tab close veto (`canCloseTab` only refuses the guide standing alone), so

dsh-md-live README · Roadmap：- [x] Write API (custom Typert Remote `mdLive/writeText`, version-checked, fenced by the Session's sandbox policy)
- [x] Editor (textarea with dirty tracking, save, and a stale-version dialog)
- [x] Code splitting (KaTeX and highlight.js languages loaded as separate chunks via `require.async`)

dsh-md-live README · Roadmap：One item is deliberately absent: **Mermaid** was measured rather than guessed: bundling it adds 11.2 MB unminified and 5.0 MB minified. Its ESM entry is only 54 KB because it splits itself into dynamic imports, and this module format has to inline every one of them. A ```` ```mermaid ```` fence therefore stays a highlighted code block with a copy control, which is a fair trade for a 5 MB engine. Even with chunk loading, the npm tarball would still carry the full ~11 MB, which every user would download regardless of whether they use Mermaid.

dsh-md-live README · Compatibility：| Piece | Requirement |
| --- | --- |
| DSH | ≥ 0.2.1-rc.2 — `sidebarRightTabs`, `sidebar.right.pane.tab`, `remote.workspaceFiles`; `typert` for the write Remote; `locale` for the copy; `require.async` for chunk loading |
| Sandbox services | The write path reads `sessions` and `sandboxPolicy` when the composition has them; without `sandboxPolicy` (plain `fs-local`) it passes no policy and keeps the backend's own behaviour |
| Desktop actions | `remote.session.openWorkspacePath` / `canOpenWorkspacePath`; the buttons hide themselves when the Host has no desktop to open them on |
| `preview_md` | The `tools` service only — the tool is a plain registry definition, so no Host package is installed into the profile |
| Math | `katex` 0.16; its minified build is imported directly, because the client bundle is deliberately not minified and the unminified entry is twice the size |
| Build | Node.js ≥ 18 |
| Runtime | React ≥ 18, supplied by DSH's browser module table and not bundled |
